newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela court ruling ratifies Placer rights - CVG.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela court ruling ratifies Placer rights - CVG.

text.p: A ruling by Venezuela's Supreme Court Tuesday on the rights to the gold-rich Las Cristinas property ratified the rights of Canada's Placer Dome Inc to develop the concession, a top government official said.

"This Court ruling reflects...that we can go ahead with the exploitation of this important deposit with the Canadian company Placer Dome," said Elias Ynaty, president of state holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG), Placer's 30 percent partner in the Cristinas venture.

Ynaty, quoted in a CVG press release, said the Supreme Court ruling confirmed the ownership rights of the CVG-Placer Dome joint venture and removed the uncertainty created by Crystallex International Corp's claim on Las Cristinas.
Ynaty added that the CVG was not concerned about Crystallex's plans to appeal Tuesday's preliminary ruling, which said the rival claim to the concession rights had been filed too late.
Crystallex lawyers on Wednesday said the court, despite Tuesday's ruling, would now examine the suit in full, and they insisted the decision was favorable.
CVG and Placer announced a $576 million joint venture to develop the gold-rich Las Cristinas property in 1994.
When the government relaxed currency controls and announced tax breaks for large industrial projects in 1996, Placer said it would start construction at the site this year.
But the process has been held up by the suit introduced by Crystallex's Venezuelan unit, Inversora Mael SA, earlier this year.
Mael acquired Las Cristinas concessions four and six in 1986 but was stripped of them by the Energy and Mines Ministry in 1989.

Ynaty added that the CVG planned to sue Mael for failing to comply with a contract it signed in 1991 in which he said it had renounced its claims to the Las Cristinas concessions and received several other mining concessions in return.

Placer has estimated Las Cristinas' reserves at more than 20 million ounces. Crystallex, which operates a small mine nearby, has said Cristinas could produce between 250,000 and 400,000 ounces of gold per year.
Venezuelan government officials have insisted throughout the dispute that Crystallex's claim is unjustified and that the joint venture in which Placer has a 70 percent stake would go ahead.
